note: Deduction guides let a class template infer its arguments from the constructor, like std::pair does.
A concept on auto reads like a type but still constrains the deduced argument at the call site.
A requires clause is a named boolean gate; the compiler rejects the overload with your message, not a wall of SFINAE.
A requires-expression checks that expressions compile; it never runs them at runtime.
The more constrained overload wins only when one concept provably subsumes the other, not merely implies it.
consteval forces evaluation at compile time; calling it with a runtime argument is a hard error.
A constexpr array lives in read-only memory once fully computed at compile time.
A constexpr function is an ordinary function that also happens to be usable in a constant expression.
Chaining CRTP mixins stacks static behaviour, each layer casting back to the full derived type.
CRTP dispatches through the derived type at compile time, so there is no vtable and no virtual call.
A custom trait is just a struct with a static constexpr value; the standard traits are no different.
auto in a return type decays like a value; decltype(auto) preserves the reference the expression has.
A trailing decltype on the expression itself is expression SFINAE, no enable_if machinery needed.
The four fold forms differ by which side the operator and the ... land on relative to the pack.
A full specialization must match the primary template's parameter list exactly.
The compiler deduces T from the argument; you only spell it out when deduction is ambiguous.
Partial specialization narrows the pattern; it must still leave at least one parameter free.
T&& in a deduced context is a forwarding reference, not an rvalue reference; std::forward restores its value category.
Each policy is an independent template parameter, so behaviour is chosen by composing types, not flags.
A substitution failure removes the overload from the set silently instead of erroring.
void_t maps any well-formed expression to void, which is the whole trick behind detection.
Tag dispatch pushes the branch into overload resolution, so no runtime if survives to the binary.
A template template parameter binds to the container itself, not to one instantiation of it.
is_same_v compares types exactly, so int and const int are already considered different.
A typelist is just a struct that never gets instantiated; all the work happens in its template arguments.
sizeof...(Args) counts the pack at compile time and costs nothing at runtime.
